approval_required_for: Any change to activation_bits, weight_bits, scale_bits, accumulator_bits, rounding mode, or saturation policy.
Any replacement of a trusted template, addition of a new template, or introduction of free-form RTL generation.
Any pipeline repartitioning or change to stage input/output/internal bit widths.
Any change to 16-bit/32-bit data-edge element_bits that affects AXI packing, transfer counts, residual joins, or memory/runtime contracts.
Any repair that changes attention GQA parameters, FFN dimensions, hidden_size, intermediate_size, target sequence bound, or lane count rather than merely binding already-approved parameters.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block evidence-gate promotion, attach failed checker evidence to the SACG record, and route only the failed template/numeric slices to bounded_template_repair; do not loosen numeric tolerance or introduce free-form RTL.
executable_actions.rationale: Complete the subtask acceptance evidence set by checking the visible stage/template matrix against the trusted template library, Stage 2 template selection, numeric policy, and parameter-binding requirements.

executable_actions.on_failure: Create a stage retry request and trust barrier for the unresolved numeric/template slice; do not promote to Stage 4 or Stage 5 until the failing checker is rerun and passes.
executable_actions.rationale: If the audit finds an untrusted template, incompatible width, missing accumulator policy, or unbound numeric parameter, repair only within trusted template and numeric-policy boundaries.

executable_actions.on_failure: Return the specific unbound parameter or incompatible template instance to pipeline_planning for bounded_template_repair; do not proceed to code generation with defaults.
executable_actions.rationale: Turn the accepted numeric/template matrix into explicit Stage 4 template parameters so later template-constrained code generation cannot infer widths, rounding, saturation, or attention/FFN dimensions implicitly.

observations: State summary reports no active SACG contamination barriers, retry requests, or backtrack requests; no current SACG-memory blocker is asserted for this numeric/template review.

Every visible stage has a template_id and source file: norm, attention, residual, ffn, and elementwise are the only stage templates named; no free-form RTL generation is claimed in the candidate artifact.

Visible checker evidence includes template_binding_static_check=pass with summary stages=9 and free_form_rtl_generation=false, and shape_numeric_contract_check=pass with elem_bits=16 and accumulator_bits=32.
The global numeric_stream_policy declares activation_bits=16, weight_bits=16, scale_bits=16, accumulator_bits=32, rounding=nearest_even, and saturation=false.

The 16-bit and 32-bit stream widths appear intentional in the visible plan: block input, residual paths, attention output, FFN down output, and block output use 32-bit elements; normalized activations, projection inputs, MLP intermediate streams, and activation_mul output use 16-bit elements.

Per-edge element_bits match adjacent per-stage numeric_contract input/output widths in the visible data_edges and stream_edges. Residual joins receive 32-bit main and skip inputs, while the MLP gate/up join receives matching 16-bit streams at width 4864.
Accumulator policy is uniform in the visible per-stage numeric_contracts: all nine stages specify accumulator_bits=32, matching numeric_stream_policy.accumulator_bits.

Parameter-binding readiness is partial: the candidate exposes template_id, source, input/output shapes, numeric bits, attention GQA fields, and symbolic formula inputs, but the detailed template metadata rows and Stage 2 template_selection contents are not visible in this prompt and must be consumed by checkers rather than assumed.

The per-stage numeric_contract fields do not repeat weight_bits, scale_bits, rounding, or saturation; Stage 4 must bind these global numeric_stream_policy fields into each applicable template instance so code generation cannot fall back to implicit defaults.

Attention is represented as one logical trusted template stage covering QKV projection, RoPE, causal GQA attention, and output projection with q_heads=14, kv_heads=2, group_size=7, head_dim=64, seq_len_bound=16; this is planning/template evidence only, not hardware pass evidence.

FFN template reuse is polymorphic across mlp_gate_proj, mlp_up_proj, and mlp_down_proj; Stage 4 must bind different input/output widths and matrix shapes for each instance without changing the trusted template boundary.

The visible checker set does not include numeric_policy_check, template_coverage_check, or parameter_binding_static_check. Because these are explicit subtask acceptance checkers, this review cannot certify full numeric/template acceptance yet.
Symbolic latency fields are correctly marked planning-only and must not be used as timing, resource, throughput, or hardware-pass evidence.
proposed_actions: Run the full numeric/template acceptance audit over the candidate stages, numeric_stream_policy, input numeric policy, template library, template metadata, design_space, and Stage 2 template_selection.

Materialize numeric_template_audit_report.json, stage_template_numeric_matrix.json, and parameter_binding_readiness_notes.json with checker status for numeric_policy_check, template_coverage_check, parameter_binding_static_check, and template_binding_static_check.

For Stage 4, bind per-template parameters for hidden_size=896, intermediate_size=4864, seq_len=16, lanes=8, accumulator_bits=32, activation/weight/scale bits=16, rounding=nearest_even, saturation=false, attention q/kv/head/RoPE fields, and each stage-specific input/output width.

If any acceptance checker fails, perform bounded_template_repair inside the trusted template library and preserve the SACG edge-width and residual/join contracts unless an approved numeric, template, or pipeline change is granted.

Do not allow Stage 5 code generation to introduce free-form RTL or implicit numeric casts; all width conversions and accumulator policies must be template parameters or trusted glue covered by checkers.
risks: Current-stage acceptance blocker: numeric_policy_check, template_coverage_check, and parameter_binding_static_check are not shown as pass or not_run, so the numeric/template handoff lacks the required checker-backed evidence set.

Template trust risk: artifact.input.template_library, artifact.input.template_metadata, and artifact.stage2.template_selection exist in the state summary, but their detailed rows are not visible here; trusted-template coverage must be established by template_coverage_check rather than inferred from template_id strings alone.

Parameter-binding risk: weight_bits, scale_bits, rounding=nearest_even, and saturation=false are global policy fields and are not repeated per stage; if Stage 4 fails to bind them into template parameters, code generation could silently use incompatible defaults.

Cross-layer width risk: changing any 16-bit/32-bit edge width would also change AXI packing, transfer_count_bytes, residual join compatibility, and memory/runtime contracts; such changes require explicit repair and approval.

Numeric downcast risk: norm outputs and projection/downstream outputs cross between 32-bit and 16-bit domains; rounding and no-saturation behavior must be bound in the templates and checked against constraint.numeric.policy.

Template-parameter risk: attention GQA fields and FFN hidden/intermediate dimensions must be bound exactly; a mismatch in num_q_heads, num_kv_heads, group_size, head_dim, hidden_size, intermediate_size, seq_len, or lanes would be a template-constrained codegen blocker.
No hardware correctness, timing/resource closure, or board pass can be claimed from this stage; only static template/numeric planning evidence is in scope.
output.summary: The visible candidate plan binds all 9 pipeline stages to named templates and shows coherent 16-bit/32-bit stream-width transitions against the per-stage numeric contracts. The provided template_binding_static_check and shape_numeric_contract_check pass evidence supports provisional template/numeric consistency, but the subtask acceptance set is incomplete because numeric_policy_check, template_coverage_check, and parameter_binding_static_check results are not shown. Do not promote the numeric/template binding handoff until those checker-backed audit artifacts are produced.
